name: granger_causality_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Certain stocks lead others in intraday price discovery — large-cap liquid names (RELIANCE, HDFCBANK) tend to move before smaller peers in the same sector (BPCL, FEDERALBNK). By computing rolling Granger causality tests on pairs of stocks (does stock A's lagged return predict stock B's future return?), we identify lead-lag relationships in real-time. When the leader moves but the follower hasn't yet responded, we trade the follower in the expected direction. The inefficiency exists because Granger causality requires econometric testing at each time step and the lead-lag relationships are dynamic (they shift based on which stock has more information flow). Retail traders use vague notions of 'sector leaders' but don't quantify the lead-lag with statistical rigor.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

conditions: Leader_Return_5 > 20 bps (leader has moved up significantly in last 5 bars)
Follower_Return_5 < 5 bps (follower has not yet responded — lag gap > 15 bps)
Follower close < follower vwap OR follower close within 5 bps of vwap (hasn't caught up)
Leader_Return_5 < -20 bps (leader has moved down significantly)
Follower_Return_5 > -5 bps (follower has not yet responded)
Follower close > follower vwap OR follower close within 5 bps of vwap

exit.signal_exit: Leader reverses direction: Leader_Return_5 changes sign

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, lead-lag relationships become unreliable (correlations spike to 1)
filters.volume_filter: Both leader and follower must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)

weaknesses: Granger causality on 60 1-min returns has low statistical power — the test may not detect genuine lead-lag with only 60 observations, leading to false negatives (missed trades) or false positives (spurious causality)
The follower may not respond because the leader's move is idiosyncratic (not sector-wide) — the gap is structural, not a lag, and the follower correctly ignores the leader's move
Short holding period (5-20 min) means the follower's response must happen quickly; in reality, some lead-lag effects take 30-60 minutes to propagate, exceeding the time stop
prior_art: Granger (1969) causality test; Lo & MacKinlay (1990) on cross-autocorrelation and lead-lag; Brennan et al. (1993) on information content; intraday lead-lag in Indian markets studied by Ullah et al.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
